core.title: Give every criteria entry id, description, harness and expected_outcome
core.given: One or more criteria entries are present. This covers new, edited and existing unchanged entries, in any artifact.
core.when: the planner authors, edits or evaluates an artifact that holds those criteria entries
core.then: Every criteria entry follows the documented shape: it has all of the required fields id, description, harness and expected_outcome.
prefer: Include all four required fields (id, description, harness, expected_outcome) when you first write the entry.
When you come across an existing criteria entry that is missing a required field, add the missing field so that it matches the documented shape.
avoid: Criteria entries that leave out any of id, description, harness or expected_outcome.
Adding extra ad-hoc fields in place of a missing required field.
core.why: Criteria are the structured form of an acceptance. Because the shape is fixed, downstream tooling can pick the harness template and resolve the expected outcome without guessing.
evidence: A reviewer confirms that every criteria entry in the artifact, including unchanged ones, has the fields id, description, harness and expected_outcome.
The disposition is documentation-only (severity 2). Compliance is established by reviewing the artifact, not by a blocking automated check.
verification: The check is field presence only: a criteria entry must carry id, description, harness and expected_outcome (the documented shape). The convention sets no rule on the content of the field values, so a check must not invent value-completeness requirements.
Disposition: documentation-only. Severity: 2. Compliance is established by reviewing the artifact, not by a blocking automated check.

Activation needs a content-level observer that detects criteria entries in any planner-authored or planner-reviewed artifact; no file-kind or path whitelist applies, and whether the entries changed is irrelevant. Until such an observer exists, activation is not deterministic from existing facts.

fires: The planner writes a new criteria entry.
The planner edits an existing criteria entry, for example by changing its harness or expected outcome.
The planner authors, revises or reviews an artifact that already holds criteria entries, even if those entries are not changed.
Any criteria entry, anywhere, lacks one of id, description, harness or expected_outcome.
doesNotFire: The artifact being authored or reviewed holds no criteria entries at all.

classification.note: Already stack-neutral: it names no artifact kind or path, and explicitly covers new, edited and unchanged entries in any artifact.
The planner is the convention's authoring role, not a stack role; no stack construct appears.
The four field names are defined by the convention's documented shape, not by any stack; the documented_shape term definition from verifier_detail[0] is inlined here.
Harness template selection and expected-outcome resolution are convention tooling concepts, stack-neutral.
Concrete field-presence move; no stack construct to neutralize.
Applies the unconditional obligation to existing entries; no stack construct.
Direct negation of the required-field set.
Gaming vector: an extra ad-hoc field never substitutes for a missing required one; extra fields alongside the four required ones remain permitted, so no obligation is added.
Review-based evidence over the artifact, stack-neutral.
Per-rule disposition (documentation-only, severity 2) belongs to core verification; the review-not-blocking-check statement is kept as evidence as well.
The field-presence-only scope and the no-rule-on-value-content limit go to core.verification; the documented_shape term definition is already inlined in core.then.
Per-rule severity and disposition are not profile keys; they are carried in core.verification.

The file_kind fact with no whitelist is already neutral. Its note (a content-level observer is needed; activation is not deterministic until it exists; no file-kind or path whitelist applies) is carried into core.verification because the neutral facts schema has no note field.

neutralityNotes: This rule is already stack-neutral in the Bun rewrite: it scopes itself to criteria entries in any artifact, its activation explicitly applies no file-kind or path whitelist, and its required fields (id, description, harness, expected_outcome) are defined by the convention's documented shape rather than by any stack, runtime or file format. Nothing needed a profile key (the core needs no path, suffix, idiom or role scoping), so profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty, and no item contains Bun-specific content, so bunOnly is empty. Per-rule severity 2 and the documentation-only disposition moved into core.verification. The activation fact keeps observability needs_new_observer: reliably finding criteria entries in arbitrary artifacts requires a content-level observer that no current stack provides, and that deference is recorded in core.verification.
